panels.visual: Athens around 620 BC: a stern lawgiver, Draco (thin, grim, long black beard), unrolling a scroll of laws in a dark hall while frightened citizens look on
panels.caption: Long ago, Athens had the laws of Draco. Almost every crime was punished with death.

panels.visual: An ancient Athenian court: a scrawny thief clutching one cabbage, a stern judge pointing, comic horror
panels.caption: Even stealing a cabbage.

panels.visual: Poor Athenian farmers in chains being led away by a rich lender with a money bag, a family crying, angry crowds gathering with sticks
panels.caption: Poor farmers who could not pay their debts were sold as slaves. Athens was close to civil war.

panels.visual: Solon (wise old man, wide straw hat, staff, grey beard) on a rocky hill above Athens being handed a scroll and a laurel by citizens, rich and poor together, golden light
panels.caption: In 594 BC both sides asked one man to fix it: Solon, poet and traveller.

panels.visual: Solon breaking chains off the Athenian farmers, who leap up rejoicing; torn debt documents flying in the wind
panels.caption: He cancelled the debts and freed everyone enslaved for debt.

panels.visual: Solon tossing Draco's scroll into a fire, keeping one small scroll labelled MURDER
panels.caption: He scrapped Draco's cruel laws, all except the law on murder.

panels.visual: A big open-air assembly of ordinary Athenian men on a hillside with a stone speaker's platform cut into the rock, one poor farmer raising his hand to vote; Solon smiling
panels.caption: And he let every citizen, even the poorest, vote in the Assembly. Later the Assembly met right here, on the Pnyx.

panels.visual: Solon on a ship leaving the harbour of Athens, waving; on the shore citizens shouting requests at him, holding scrolls
panels.caption: Then everyone wanted changes. So he made Athens swear to keep his laws, and sailed away for ten years.

panels.visual: A glittering treasure hall in Sardis: heaps of gold and gems; Croesus, king of Lydia (plump, jewelled, proud) showing it all off to the travelling Solon
panels.caption: In Lydia he met King Croesus, the richest man in the world.

speech.speaker: Croesus
speech.text: Who is the happiest man alive?

panels.visual: Solon calmly shaking his head while Croesus, who expected his own name, goes red; inset, a simple Athenian soldier, Tellus, with his grandchildren
panels.caption: Solon named Tellus, an ordinary Athenian who saw his grandchildren grow and died bravely for his city.

speech.speaker: Solon
speech.text: Call no man happy until he is dead.

panels.visual: Years later: Croesus, captured by the Persian king Cyrus, tied on top of a great pyre of logs as the fire is lit, crying out to the sky; Cyrus watching from his horse
panels.caption: Years later Cyrus of Persia took his kingdom and put him on a burning pyre.

panels.visual: Cyrus raising his hand to stop the fire while servants throw water; a sudden thunderstorm of rain pouring down on the pyre; Glauka in a corner holding a tiny sign 'the dates don't fit'
panels.caption: Cyrus heard why, remembered he was only a man too, and ordered the fire put out. Then rain finished the job.
